newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: CRICKET - Rixon welcomes Kennedy with enthusiasm.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET - Rixon welcomes Kennedy with enthusiasm.

text.p: SAHIWAL, Nov 18 - The loss of experienced fast bowler Danny Morrison is a huge blow to the New Zealand cricket team's chances in the test series against Pakistan, but coach Steve Rixon greeted the naming of his replacement with enthusiasm, NZPA reported on Tuesday (NZT).

Raw Otago fast bowler Robert Kennedy has been drafted into the tour party after Morrison broke down with a long-standing groin injury, which failed to pass a fitness test on the second day of New Zealand's three-day match against a Pakistan President's 11.
Morrison's impending departure robs the Kiwis of their main strike bowler, who has played 47 tests.
His misfortune was a stroke of luck for Kennedy, 24, who questioned his readiness for international status in the latter stages of the tour of the West Indies last April.
Rixon watched Kennedy bowl in four pre-season matches at the New Zealand Cricket Academy in Christchurch last month and came away impressed.
"I thought he did a fantastic job in those matches and I am pleased he has a chance although the circumstances with Danny going home are obviously disappointing.
"Robert has genuine pace and he will be used in a striking role.
"He won't be nurtured but we will show a bit of leniency towards him," Rixon said.
Kennedy was plagued by no-ball problems and a tendency to spray the ball about when he was elevated to the international game for the first time last summer.
"I understand there was a fair deal of pressure on him, by several forces last year, with probably the most coming from himself.
"I just want him to be relaxed as possible going into any given match. I want him to bowl fast and enjoy himself," Rixon said.
"If it doesn't happen on the day there won't be any ostracism, there will be encouragement.
"He's a kid of the future and I think he will do well."

The first test against Pakistan starts in Lahore on Thursday, and Rixon hinted Kennedy might arrive too late to be seriously considered for that match, which is followed by the second test and three one-day internationals.
"I'm unsure whether he'll be considered for the first test, although it certainly seems impractical at this stage.
"But there are so many holes at the moment that we have to work out which ones are the right ones to fill."
Rixon said Morrison's forced departure was a blow.
"He's our main strike bowler, he has a lot of experience and he plays an important role off the field because he has such a good rapport with all the players.
"Just having him around the players is important, but we need him 110 percent fit all the time and that's going to take time now."

Morrison is to consult Christchurch surgeon Paul Armour, who operated on his groin in June, for a full assessment on the extent of damage. He is hoping to play for Auckland before the end of this month.
